newsitem.title: UK: UK SIB sets new pensions misselling measures.
newsitem.headline: UK SIB sets new pensions misselling measures.

text.p: Britain's financial markets watchdog, the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), on Tuesday announced a set of measures designed to speed up the review of the misselling of pensions by banks and insurance companies.

It said the 24 firms with the greatest number of cases had been set demanding new targets for the completion of the review by the regulator of the pensions industry, the Personal Investment Authority (PIA).
Pension misselling has affected several hundred thousand people who may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions by financial companies during the late 1980s and early 1990s.
The review into the misselling was launched by the SIB in 1994 but progress has been slow.
"Last November I said that the front line regulators would agree targets with their firms. I welcome the fact that these targets have now been set," said SIB Chairman Sir Andrew Large in a statement.
"The excuses have to stop. Firms can be under no illusion that results are expected from them, and expected soon," he added.

The SIB said failure to meet the new targets could provide grounds for disciplinary action, adding that it was providing new criteria for the giving of guarantees by pensions firms to provide redress to customers. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
